items.notes: Passage covers only outcome metrics and CI/threshold definitions; nothing states compute, workspace, or access are held identical across arms.
States held-out task performance is the primary outcome, final artifacts are evaluated on a held-out test set with a pre-registered rubric, and no held-out feedback flows back to the arms.
Explicitly names LLM non-determinism and prescribes repeated runs / multiple random seeds per task with a variance-components model over within-task variance.
Says each task is evaluated on both arms 'under identical compute budgets', but the passage is silent on workspace and access parity, so only part of the requirement is visible.
Allocates K=2-3 repeats per cell with new random seeds and fits a mixed model with an explicit within-cell replication variance term.
Eval set is pre-constructed, pre-registered before optimization and locked with a recorded hash, but no passage states that held-out evaluation is opened only after the candidate harness is frozen.
States the model version is pinned across conditions so no native model capability drift can explain the gain, isolating harness from model improvement.
Explicitly requires the scoring service to run outside the candidate workspace and snapshots to be stored externally, noting in-workspace scoring would be circular.
Logging covers trajectories, judge versions, timestamps and hyperparameters, but no passage meters compute, tokens, cost, or call budget per candidate.
Passages establish a held-out set and out-of-workspace evaluation but say nothing about freezing the candidate before the held-out set is opened.
Uses a permutation test against a shuffled-label null plus bootstrap CIs and effect size, explicitly framed as distinguishing the shift from random rating noise.
Decomposes agreement change into named rater-level variance sources (within-rater resampling, severity drift, halo) via paired variance-component analysis, not item variance alone.
States directly that the same N items are scored by both the human and the automatic rater under both the original and revised rubric.
Unit is (item, human-rater, automatic-rater) triples with raters drawn from a fixed pool, but the passages never state that rater variance is modelled or accounted for in analysis.
Requires replicate human ratings from a rater pool and a balanced or recoverable crossed-random-effects design, which treats raters as a variance source alongside items.
The design is built around preventing overfitting-via-evaluation and includes a train/held-out eval split ablation testing whether reported gains generalize.
Defines an explicit Target-Set Inflation overfitting ratio (target vs test score) and a hypothesis/test comparing target-set and test-set scores across budget regimes.
Records software/library versions and states the optimizer config is fixed with only the stopping rule differing, but no passage says the scored candidate's own version is recorded.
Contradicts the requirement: condition C2's stopping rule reads the held-out test score during the run to decide when to stop.
A 'RandomSampler' agent and an 'Agents and Baselines' section appear, but the passage frames RandomSampler as a gamer rather than a non-optimizing reference and its description is cut off.
Passage only enumerates optimizer agents and an exhaustive verification baseline; nothing states the held-out test is isolated from or unreachable by the agent.

A reserved 5-problem held-out set is re-scored post-hoc and rankings compared, but this is framed as validating the saturation threshold, so whether it checks target-evaluation overfitting is ambiguous.
States that test outcomes on held-out artifacts update the hypothesis probability through a validation gate, placing the decision on held-out results.
States the held-out evaluation set is used with no training or optimization inside that run, i.e. the candidate is not changed while the held-out set is open.
The unit tuple includes two human raters per item, which would permit rater-variance estimation, but nothing in the passage states that rater variation is actually accounted for.
